newsitem.title: USA: U.S. may challenge California ballot initiative.
newsitem.headline: U.S. may challenge California ballot initiative.

text.p: The Justice Department is considering a legal challenge to California's recently approved ballot initiative aimed at dismantling affirmative action programmes, the White House said Wednesday.
Spokesman Mike McCurry said the Justice Department had asked the White House for additional time to consider the legal basis for a challenge to the state's initiative.

President Clinton has expressed opposition to California's Proposition 209, preferring instead his own "mend it, not end it" prescription for reforming affirmative action programmes aimed at giving minorities and women equal job opportunities.

The measure bars discrimination and preferential treatment based on race or sex in public employment, education and contracting in California, effectively outlawing government affirmative action programmes used to broaden opportunities for women and minorities.
Many senior administration lawyers believe the new law could undermine federal civil rights policy and cause other states to follow California's lead.
A federal judge in San Francisco is to hear arguments Dec. 16 from civil rights groups who are seeking to stop the University of California from implementing the initiative.

It will be up to Clinton, based on Attorney General Janet Reno's recommendations, to decide whether the federal government should join in challenging the proposition. The ballot was approved overwhelmingly Nov. 5 by California voters who also gave Clinton a lopsided victory in their state.

"Of course the president has been opposed and expressed his opposition, reiterated his opposition publicly yesterday," McCurry said. "That's not the issue here. The issue is whether there are legal grounds for a constitutional challenge."
